output.title: When redaction stops being a habit and becomes a workflow
output.body:
If you keep redacting the same names, IDs, or fields, the question is not whether AI can do it. The question is whether this is still a one-off habit, or a recurring workflow worth looking at.

For an owner-operator, the practical test is simple: do you see the same redaction pattern weekly or more often, and does it pull you away from revenue work or lead follow-up? If not, keep it manual. If yes, treat it as a bounded workflow decision, not a vague automation project.

That is also where the control matters. Final approval stays with you. A redaction workflow should not send or store a document until a human has reviewed the output. And if the material is highly sensitive, such as legal, medical, or financial work, Bareni currently treats that as out of scope rather than forcing automation into the wrong place.

If you want a clean next step, write down three things: what gets redacted, how often it happens, and which tool it lives in. That usually tells you whether you have a redaction habit, or a workflow worth examining.
